situation: A friend of Aboubakar's family wants to move to Buea to start a large farm, because the soil there is very fertile.
Another friend warns him: "It is dangerous! You will live on the side of an active volcano." The family friend is confused. Is living near Mount Cameroon a good opportunity or a great risk?
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that the family friend does not know if living near Mount Cameroon is a good opportunity or a great risk.
Why does he want to farm near Buea?
He wants to farm there because the volcanic soil is very fertile.
What should he do before moving?
He should learn about the dangers, choose a safe place away from old lava flows, and know the evacuation plans.

qa.q: What did the lava flows of Mount Cameroon do in 1999 and 2000?
qa.a: They destroyed farms, forest and part of the road between Limbe and Idenau, and threatened villages.

qa.q: In 1986, a cloud of gas came out of Lake Nyos. What happened?
qa.a: A cloud of carbon dioxide came out of the lake and flowed down the valleys. About 1,700 people and thousands of animals died.
Other hazards are ash falls, poisonous gases, mudflows (lahars), earthquakes and landslides.

sum.title: I. Volcanic Hazards
defs: A volcanic hazard is a danger caused by a volcano to people and property.
items: A. Lava Flows and Ash
– Lava flows burn and bury farms, houses and roads (Mount Cameroon, 1999 and 2000).
– Ash falls cover crops, pollute water, cause breathing problems and make roofs collapse.
B. Gases, Mudflows and Earthquakes
– Poisonous gases kill people and animals: Lake Monoun (1984, 37 deaths) and Lake Nyos (1986, about 1,700 deaths).
– Mudflows (lahars) of ash and rainwater bury valleys.
– Eruptions cause earthquakes and landslides.

qa.q: Why are the soils around Mount Cameroon very fertile?
qa.a: Volcanic rocks and ash break down into soils rich in minerals. They support plantations of bananas, tea, rubber and oil palm.
In volcanic areas, underground heat turns water into steam, which turns turbines. This is geothermal energy, used in Iceland and in Kenya.

qa.q: Give two other benefits of volcanoes.
qa.a: Volcanoes attract tourists, like the Mount Cameroon Race of Hope. They also give building materials (basalt, pozzolana) and new land.

sum.title: II. Importance of Volcanoes
sum.intro: Volcanoes are also useful to people:
items: Benefits
– Fertile soils for agriculture: plantations of the Cameroon Development Corporation (CDC) around Mount Cameroon.
– Geothermal energy (Iceland, Kenya) and hot springs.
– Tourism: the Race of Hope, mountain hiking and crater lakes.
– Building materials: basalt and pozzolana (volcanic ash for cement).
– New land formed by lava.

qa.q: What can scientists do before an eruption?
qa.a: They can monitor the volcano with instruments that measure earthquakes, gases and the swelling of the ground, and give warnings.

qa.q: What did Cameroon do to prevent another disaster at Lake Nyos?
qa.a: Pipes were placed in Lake Nyos (from 2001) and in Lake Monoun to release the gas slowly and safely.

sum.title: III. Adaptation, Mitigation and Preventive Measures
sum.intro: People cannot stop eruptions, but they can reduce the risk:
items: Measures
– Monitoring and warning: observe earthquakes, gases and ground swelling.
– Evacuation plans and drills; safe shelters.
– Hazard maps and land-use rules: no houses on old lava paths.
– Strong, sloping roofs to shed ash.
– Degassing pipes in dangerous lakes (Nyos, Monoun).
– Education of the population on safety rules.

evaluation: Lava flows and poisonous gases (also ash falls and mudflows).
Why do many people live near Mount Cameroon despite the danger?
They live there because the volcanic soils are very fertile and give good harvests.
How was Lake Nyos made safer?
Pipes were placed in the lake to release the carbon dioxide slowly.
remediation: A danger caused by a volcano is a volcanic ______.
The Lake Nyos disaster happened in ______.
The gas released by Lake Nyos was carbon ______.
Heat from volcanic areas gives ______ energy.
Watching a volcano with instruments is called ______.
end.homework: Ask your parents if they have ever felt the ground shake. Write where and when it happened, and what they felt.
teacherNote: Correction 1: the source notes say volcanoes bring up granite. Granite is an intrusive rock that cools deep underground; we see it only after erosion. Diamonds, however, are brought up by old volcanic pipes (kimberlite).
Correction 2: Lake Nyos (21 August 1986, about 1,700 deaths) and Lake Monoun (15 August 1984, 37 deaths) were added: they are the most deadly volcanic hazards in Cameroon.
Degassing pipes: Lake Nyos from 2001, Lake Monoun from 2003.
